slides.say: Which of the following statements is not necessarily true?

Four statements, and one of them is not necessarily true. That means it can fail for some shape. [short pause] So we go statement by statement. Anything that's surely true, we cross out, and we hope to be left with one.

[short pause] Statement one, every rhombus is a deltoid. What does that mean? Every rhombus has everything a deltoid is guaranteed to have. A deltoid has two pairs of equal sides, and in each pair the equal sides are next to each other.

A rhombus has all four sides equal. So the two top sides are equal and next to each other, and so are the two bottom sides. That's two pairs, so every rhombus is a deltoid. It's true, so choice number one is out. Not every deltoid is a rhombus, by the way. But a deltoid with all four sides equal is a rhombus.
at: A rhombus has all four sides equal
so choice number one is out

slides.say: Statement two, every square is a rectangle. A rectangle has its opposite sides equal and all its angles ninety. A square has all that, and more, because all its sides are equal. It's like an upgraded rectangle. So it's true, and choice number two is out. Not every rectangle is a square, because its sides don't have to be all equal.
at: A rectangle has its opposite sides
and choice number two is out

slides.say: Statement three, every rectangle is a parallelogram. A parallelogram has its opposite sides equal and parallel, its opposite angles equal, and neighbouring angles that add up to one hundred eighty. A rectangle has all of these. So it's true, and choice number three is out. The other way around isn't true, because not every parallelogram has four right angles.
at: A parallelogram has its opposite sides
and choice number three is out

slides.say: Three statements are out. On the exam, you'd mark choice number four without checking it. Since we're in a lesson, let's check it anyway. Every parallelogram has perpendicular diagonals.

Perpendicular diagonals are a property of the rhombus, and not every parallelogram has them. Take a rectangle, nine by four. It's a parallelogram. If its diagonals were perpendicular, it would be a rhombus, and a rectangle that's a rhombus is a square. This one is not a square, so its diagonals are not perpendicular. One shape where it fails is enough, so this statement is not necessarily true. Choice number four is our answer. [pause] Okay. I'll see you in the next question.
at: Choice number four is our answer
